text:
Jess H: Heads-up — customer (acme-pay) opened a ticket saying behavior changed right after last canary. They see stale persona/formatting in responses even though model version rolled. Example: input "Summarize the Q1 sync" used to return an action-oriented summary, now returns a long policy-style paragraph. :confused:

Jess H: Minimal repro they sent: request_id=abc123, request_id=abc124. They call the hosted endpoint with X-Model-Version: redwood-rlhf-v2 and include a prefix in metadata (system prompt).

Jess H: From our logs: several responses show cache hit on KV key `prefix:session:acme-qa:abc123` at time ~2023-11-12T14:22:10Z while model-version header is v2. The cache hit metadata has model_tag=v1. Suspect prefix/KV entries not being invalidated or remapped when we switched routing to v2 canary.

Mike (support): Thanks, Jess. Can you paste the exact curl they used and the matching server logs (masking creds)? Also are they routed via the new smart-router or pinned to dedicated pool?

Jess H: Curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "X-Model-Version: redwood-rlhf-v2" \n  -d '{"input":"Summarize the Q1 sync","metadata":{"prefix":"system:be-brisk-v2"}}'
```
Logs (sanitized):
```
[14:22:09] router: route->pool(dedicated-us-east-1)
[14:22:10] kvcache: get key=prefix:session:acme-qa:abc123 -> HIT (model_tag=v1, expires=2023-12-01T00:00:00Z)
[14:22:10] runtime: selected model redwood-rlhf-v2
[14:22:10] response: served from cache_prefix_v1_format
```

Anita M: @Jess H — this looks like the prefix->model_tag mapping wasn't updated during the canary rollout. We changed router policy to prefer v2 for 20% traffic but the cache namespace uses model_tag-scoped keys. If the mapping isn't migrated or keys aren't invalidated, you can serve v2 requests with v1 cached prefix tokens.

Anita M: Quick repro I ran on staging: create prefix key under model_tag=v1, then issue request with header model=v2 -> observed same mismatch. Repro steps: 1) write kv prefix key `prefix:session:test:xyz` with tag=v1, 2) call endpoint with X-Model-Version=v2, 3) observe runtime logs show cache HIT tagged v1 and output uses legacy formatting.

Anita M: Short-term mitigation: evict affected prefix keys for the customer. Admin API to evict:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/kv/evict \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>' \n  -d '{"keys": ["prefix:session:acme-qa:abc123","prefix:session:acme-qa:abc124"]}'
```

Evan S: Confirmed the canary rollout included a router change last night 02:11 UTC that flipped routing weights but we didn't version the cache namespace. Deploy log: deploy-bot: canary/redwood-rlhf-v2 @ 2023-11-12T02:11:03Z :rocket:. I'll patch router to include model_tag in cache key or invalidate keys on variant change.

Mike (support): I'll tell the customer we evicted the keys and ask them to retry. Please post here when patch is up and we can close ticket. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary/redwood-rlhf-v2 deployed by ci:jenkins at 2023-11-12T02:11:03Z (sha: a1b2c3). Rollout target: 20% traffic.

Jess H: Thanks — will update ticket after customer verifies. Creating a follow-up internal issue to make prefix cache namespace robust: INC-3947.

Anita M: Long-term: we'll either include model_tag in key or add a cache-version header that forces remap on rollout. Also add an automated invalidation step in rollouts that touch prefix behavior.

Evan S: I'll post a PR with the key-change by EOD and schedule a hotfix rollout.

Mike (support): Customer update: "We retried and responses now match expected format." Marking as escalated -> resolved pending root cause fix.

Jess H: Closing loop here, creating postmortem stub and linking to INC-3947. Thanks all. :heart:
